corrections: 【引用元数据】修正前:『Nature 628, 29-30, 2024-03』把卷页与月份绑在一起 → 修正后:应写成『在线发表 2024-03-29;印刷版 Nature 628, 29–30(第 8006 期,2024-04-04)』。一手 PDF 页眉逐字为『29 March 2024』+『doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-024-00902-2』;而 Nature 卷 628 第 8006 期的封面日期是 2024-04-04(nature.com/nature/volumes/628/issues/8006)。即 29–30 页属于四月刊,不属于三月。引用时二者必须分开标注,不能写成『628, 29-30 (2024-03)』。

【(b) 的构句口径】修正前:把『there is no evidence that using these platforms is rewiring children's brains or driving an epidemic of mental illness』当作 Odgers 的独立断言句 → 修正后:它是从属分句,原文为『Two things can be independently true about social media. First, that there is no evidence that... Second, that considerable reforms to these platforms are required, given how much time young people spend on them.』位于小标题『A generation in crisis』之下。逐字引用需保留『First, that…』的从句形态,且单独摘引前半句而略去『Second, that considerable reforms… are required』会把 Odgers 误框成为平台辩护——她在同一段明确主张需要『considerable reforms』。Haidt 在 X 上的反驳正是只摘前半句。

【(c) 的截断】修正前:以『…use such platforms more often...』省略号收尾 → 修正后:原句完整结尾为『…use such platforms more often or in different ways from their healthy peers¹.』(带文献标注 1),且紧接在『Most data are correlative.』之后。若只引到 more often,会丢掉 Odgers 的第二个机制(使用方式差异,而非仅频率),这是她论点的实质部分。

【(d) 标题与开篇句易混】修正前:把『Two things need to be said...』当成可能的标题版本之一 → 修正后:『Two things need to be said after reading The Anxious Generation.』是正文第一句(书名斜体),不是标题;标题是『The great rewiring: is social media really behind an epidemic of teenage mental illness?』,副标题(Nature 编辑撰写、非 Odgers)是『The evidence is equivocal on whether screen time is to blame for rising levels of teen depression and anxiety — and rising hysteria could distract us from tackling the real causes.』引用时须区分作者句与编辑副标题。
evidence_notes: 一手全文(Nature 原始排版 PDF,含 nature 刊头、DOI、日期、脚注编号)取自 UW–Madison PSY 532 课程镜像:https://internet.psych.wisc.edu/wp-content/uploads/532-Master/532-UnitPages/Unit-11/Odgers_Nature_2024.pdf —— 已本地读取逐字比对(注意页尾标注『This article has been excerpted for PSY 532』,即节选版,见 unresolved)。

(a) 逐字成立。原文第二句后半:『Second, the book's repeated suggestion that digital technologies are rewiring our children's brains and causing an epidemic of mental illness is not supported by science.』紧接『Worse, the bold proposal that social media is to blame might distract us from effectively responding to the real causes of the current mental-health crisis in young people.』待验措辞与一手完全一致(含 our children's brains 的物主代词、an epidemic 的不定冠词)。

(b) 逐字成立。原文:『Two things can be independently true about social media. First, that there is no evidence that using these platforms is rewiring children's brains or driving an epidemic of mental illness.』注意此处是 children's brains(无 our),与 (a) 的 our children's brains 不同——两句不可互换。

(c) 逐字成立。原文:『Most data are correlative. When associations over time are found, they suggest not that social-media use predicts or causes depression, but that young people who already have mental-health problems use such platforms more often or in different ways from their healthy peers¹.』连字符须保留:social-media use、mental-health problems。
(c) 上文一句一手作『Our efforts have produced a mix of no, small and mixed associations.』(英式,无 Oxford comma)。二手转载(kidsplaytech 汇编页)作『no, small, and mixed』——若沿用二手会引入非逐字的逗号偏差。
(d) 逐字成立。开篇句:『Two things need to be said after reading The Anxious Generation.』(The Anxious Generation 斜体)。作者署名 By Candice L. Odgers。

(e) 成立。『the kids are not all right』不出现在该 Nature 书评中;它是 Clare Morell 书评的标题全文:『The Kids Are Not All Right: A Review of Jonathan Haidt's The Anxious Generation』,Public Discourse 2024-04-24 首发(https://www.thepublicdiscourse.com/2024/04/94753/),并转载于 EPPC(https://eppc.org/publication/the-kids-are-not-all-right-a-review-of-jonathan-haidts-the-anxious-generation/)及作者 Substack。Morell 文中确有链接指向 Odgers 的 Nature 书评但未直接引用其原句,故不存在『Odgers 说过这话』的合理来源路径。
独立镜像交叉验证(a)(c)(d):Pixel Envy 书评汇总页(pxlnv.com/linklog/anxious-generation-review/)、shoresofacademia Substack、kidsplaytech 汇编页,三处引文与一手 PDF 一致。

利益相关检查:Odgers 本人在文中披露立场——『As a psychologist who has studied children's and adolescents' mental health for the past 20 years…』及『As a parent of adolescents…』,即她是该领域主要研究者之一(文中自称 hundreds of researchers, myself included),对『大效应不存在』这一结论有学术既得利益;反方 Haidt 亦有书籍销售利益。双方均非中立,应并列呈现。

反证检索:未发现 Nature 对该书评发布任何 correction / erratum / editor's note。Nature 后续刊出了三封读者来信作为对话(d41586-024-01488-5、d41586-024-01489-4、d41586-024-01040-5),属正常学术往还而非更正。Haidt 于 2024-03-30 在 X 及 afterbabel.com 公开反驳,称其已汇集 22 项实验研究(16 项发现显著危害证据)与 9 项准实验(8 项发现危害证据)——这是对『no evidence』强措辞的实质性争议,引用 (b) 时宜同时点明该争议存在,但它不构成对 Odgers 原文措辞的推翻。

Odgers。页脚注明 "This article has been excerpted for PSY 532"。

(d) 开篇句逐字核对成立:原文第一句为 "Two things need to be said after reading The Anxious Generation."(书名为斜体)。后接 "First, this book is going to sell a lot of copies, because Jonathan Haidt is telling a scary story about children's development that many parents are primed to believe." 该开篇段另由独立来源 pxlnv.com 的书评汇编逐字复现,两处一致。

(b) 逐字核对成立:原文 "A generation in crisis" 小标题下为 "Two things can be independently true about social media. First, that there is no evidence that using these platforms is rewiring children's brains or driving an epidemic of mental illness. Second, that considerable reforms to these platforms are required, given how much time young people spend on them." 待验片段与之逐词一致。旁证:Haidt 本人在 X 上引用该句反驳时的措辞与此完全相同(https://x.com/JonHaidt/status/1774571680511508601)。

(c) 反向因果句逐字核对成立:"When associations over time are found, they suggest not that social-media use predicts or causes depression, but that young people who already have mental-health problems use such platforms more often or in different ways from their healthy peers."(句末带文献标注 1)。注意 "social-media" 作定语时带连字符、"mental-health problems" 带连字符。该句另由第三方独立文档 https://kidsplaytech.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Panic_First_Evidence_Later.html 逐字复现,与 PDF 完全一致(两个独立镜像互证)。

(e) 成立:"The Kids Are Not All Right" 是 Clare Morell 书评的标题,非 Odgers 用语。一手确认 https://www.thepublicdiscourse.com/2024/04/94753/ —— 标题 "The Kids Are Not All Right: A Review of Jonathan Haidt's The Anxious Generation",作者 Clare Morell,刊于 Public Discourse,2024-04-24;EPPC 同文转载 https://eppc.org/publication/the-kids-are-not-all-right-a-review-of-jonathan-haidts-the-anxious-generation/;作者本人 Substack 亦有转载。Morell 系 EPPC 技术与人的繁荣项目主任,立场与 Haidt 同向(赞成书中论点),与 Odgers 书评方向相反,故两者绝不可混引。

书目信息经两条独立路径互证:ADS 记录 bibcode 2024Natur.628...29O(https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024Natur.628...29O/abstract)与 RePEc 记录 v628y2024i8006(https://ideas.repec.org/a/nat/nature/v628y2024i8006d10.1038_d41586-024-00902-2.html)一致给出 Nature 628, 29–30 (2024), issue 8006。Nature 自家两篇读者来信 d41586-024-01488-5 与 d41586-024-01489-4 在正文中引作 "Nature 628, 29–30; 2024",系出版方自证。

未检索到 Nature 对该书评发布任何 correction / erratum / editor's note。针对性搜索无结果;敌意方来源(shoresofacademia Substack 的多篇系列批评文,含 "The Alternate Reality of Candice Odgers")亦未主张存在事实性错误或已发勘误,其攻击点是 Odgers 对既有证据的解读与取舍(称其忽略重度使用者的风险升高),而非引文或数据本身失实。这一点反向支持 (a)-(d) 文本的真实性:最有动机挑错的批评者逐字引用了同样的句子。

利益相关性提示(不影响逐字核验结论,但引用时应披露):Odgers 在文中自陈 "Hundreds of researchers, myself included, have searched for the kind of large effects suggested by Haidt" —— 她是被 Haidt 批评的那一派研究者本人,属当事方而非中立第三方;文末她另称 "As a parent of adolescents"。对照面 Morell 属倡导限制儿童使用智能手机的政策智库(EPPC),同样非中立。两边引用都应标明立场。

corrections: 无口径修正。(a)-(e) 五点全部经一手逐字核对成立,引语一字不差,书目信息 (Nature 628, 29-30, 2024) 与发表日期 (2024-03-29) 均确认。以下 evidence_notes 中的若干条为「使用警告 / 精度补充」,不是对论断本身的修正 —— 论断如实陈述,不应改写。
evidence_notes: 【一手来源确认】Candice L. Odgers, "The great rewiring: is social media really behind an epidemic of teenage mental illness?", Nature 628, 29-30 (2024), Published 29 March 2024, doi:10.1038/d41586-024-00902-2。https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-024-00902-2 (nature.com 有 idp.nature.com cookie 重定向墙,需跟随 303→302 链并带 code 参数才能取到全文)。第二独立镜像:UW-Madison PSY 532 课程 PDF https://internet.psych.wisc.edu/wp-content/uploads/532-Master/532-UnitPages/Unit-11/Odgers_Nature_2024.pdf(页眉「29 March 2024」+ doi,但末行注明 "This article has been excerpted for PSY 532",为节选本,不能用于证明任何措辞的「不存在」)。第三来源:ADS 书目 2024Natur.628...29O;RePEc v628 y2024 i8006。

【(a) 逐字核对:成立】一手原文(第一段):"Second, the book's repeated suggestion that digital technologies are rewiring our children's brains and causing an epidemic of mental illness is not supported by science." 论断所引部分自 "the book's repeated suggestion..." 起,与原文逐字完全一致(含 "our children's brains" 的 our、"is not supported by science" 的单数系动词)。原文该句前有 "Second, ",后紧接 "Worse, the bold proposal that social media is to blame might distract us from effectively responding to the real causes of the current mental-health crisis in young people."

【(b) 逐字核对:成立】一手原文("A generation in crisis" 小节首段):"Two things can be independently true about social media. First, that there is no evidence that using these platforms is rewiring children's brains or driving an epidemic of mental illness. Second, that considerable reforms to these platforms are required, given how much time young people spend on them." 论断所引与原文逐字一致(注意此处是 "children's brains" 无 our,与 (a) 处的 "our children's brains" 不同 —— 两句措辞确有细微差别,论断两处都引对了)。

【(b) 使用警告(重要)】这是全文被去语境化最严重的一句。它是 Odgers 刻意构造的「两件事可以同时成立」对句的前半;她紧接着写 "considerable reforms to these platforms are required"。单引前半会让读者误以为 Odgers 认为社媒无害/无需监管,这与她原意相反。任何引用 (b) 的正文都应同时带上 Second 分句,或至少注明其为对句前半。

【(c) 逐字核对:成立】一手原文(第三段):"Hundreds of researchers, myself included, have searched for the kind of large effects suggested by Haidt. Our efforts have produced a mix of no, small and mixed associations. Most data are correlative. When associations over time are found, they suggest not that social-media use predicts or causes depression, but that young people who already have mental-health problems use such platforms more often or in different ways from their healthy peers[ref 1]." 论断引文至 "use such platforms more often..." 为止,已用省略号标注截断,截断前逐字一致。
【(c) 使用警告】省略号截掉的是 "or in different ways from their healthy peers"。Odgers 的反向因果表述是双支的 —— 不只是「用得更频繁」(频率),还有「用法不同」(方式)。只引 "more often" 会把她的构念窄化为纯剂量效应。该句原文带文献编号 1(即她引的纵向研究证据),不是无出处断言。

【(d) 开篇句:成立,即为 "Two things need to be said..."】一手全文正文第一句逐字为:"Two things need to be said after reading The Anxious Generation."(The Anxious Generation 为斜体)。紧随其后:"First, this book is going to sell a lot of copies, because Jonathan Haidt is telling a scary story about children's development that many parents are primed to believe." 注意全文另有一处高度相似的平行句 "Two things can be independently true about social media."(见 (b)),二者极易混淆,核对时须区分:need to be said = 开篇;can be independently true = "A generation in crisis" 小节。另,标题下的 standfirst(非正文首句)为:"The evidence is equivocal on whether screen time is to blame for rising levels of teen depression and anxiety — and rising hysteria could distract us from tackling the real causes."

【(e) 确认短语不在该书评中:成立】对 nature.com 全文做了两次独立取回并定向检索 "kids" / "all right" / "alright",两次均返回无该短语。全文仅三个标题层级:主标题 "The great rewiring: is social media really behind an epidemic of teenage mental illness?"、小节 "A complex problem"、小节 "A generation in crisis" —— 无任何 "kids are not all right" 字样。全文末段逐字为:"A third truth is that we have a generation in crisis and in desperate need of the best of what science and evidence-based solutions can offer. Unfortunately, our time is being spent telling stories that are unsupported by research and that do little to support young people who need, and deserve, more."

【(e) 归属确认】"The Kids Are Not All Right" 确为 Clare Morell 书评标题,全称 "The Kids Are Not All Right: A Review of Jonathan Haidt's The Anxious Generation",首发 Public Discourse,2024-04-24,https://www.thepublicdiscourse.com/2024/04/94753/;EPPC 转载 https://eppc.org/publication/the-kids-are-not-all-right-a-review-of-jonathan-haidts-the-anxious-generation/;作者本人 Substack 亦有。Morell 身份为 EPPC(Ethics and Public Policy Center)Technology and Human Flourishing Project 主任。关键立场对比:Morell 的书评是**支持** Haidt 的(认为他已证明智能手机/社媒有害,并主张比 Haidt 更强硬的政策),与 Odgers 的批评性书评立场相反 —— 把这个标题误挂到 Odgers 名下会造成立场倒置,这正是该论断要防的错误,防得对。

【利益相关性检查】Nature 页面载明 "The author declares no competing interests." Odgers 的机构关系在文中作者简介里已自行披露:UC Irvine 心理科学与信息学教授、研究副院长;co-leads 加拿大 CIFAR(Child & Brain Development 项目)与瑞士 Jacobs Foundation 的国际儿童发展网络。补充事实:Jacobs Foundation 曾向 UC Irvine 拨款约 1100 万美元支持 CERES(Connecting the EdTech Research Ecosystem),由 Odgers 参与共同领导,该项目部分工作与产业界合作。未检索到任何来自科技平台公司(Meta/Google 等)的直接资助记录,也未检索到针对她的正式利益冲突指控或调查。结论:披露完整,无隐瞒,但读者可自行判断 EdTech 生态资助是否构成软性倾向。

对「短语不存在」的证明本质上是负面证据。我做了两次独立的 nature.com 全文取回,均报告无 "the kids are not all right"。但需说明一个已知瑕疵:其中一次对单词 "kids" 的检索返回 NONE,而全文实际含 Haidt 引语 "a firehose of addictive content that entered through kids' eyes and ears"(在引号内),说明取回层的关键词检索并非 100% 可靠。web.archive.org 在本环境被封禁,无法用 Wayback 快照(存在 20260723034521 快照)做第三次交叉验证。综合判断:(e) 成立的置信度高(短语的正面归属已由 Morell 三个独立站点确证),但严格意义上的「全文穷尽检索」只到两次。
